Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import os,glob,re,json
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
gi=G['Demo pair 1 input']; go=G['Demo pair 1 output']
bg=5
from collections import Counter
cells=[(i,j) for i in range(len(gi)) for j in range(len(gi[0])) if gi[i][j]!=bg]
print(cells)
go_cells={(i,j) for i in range(len(go)) for j in range(len(go[0])) if go[i][j]!=bg}
diff=sorted(go_cells-set(cells))
print(diff, {gi[i][j] for i,j in diff})

    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]

    return G

from collections import Counter

def f(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0]); o=[r[:] for r in g]; bg=Counter(v for r in g for v in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    dirs=[(-1,-1),(1,1)]   # main diag dirs to traverse

        res=[]

            i=j+1

    for r in range(h):

    # group non-bg cells by diagonal lines
    lines={}; used=set()
    for r in range(h):

            lines.setdefault((r-c),[]).append((r,c,v)); lines.setdefault((r+c),[]).append((r,c,v))
    changed=True

        for key,L in list(lines.items()):

            # collect full lines for this geometry: need cells sorted along direction
            pts=sorted([p for _,_,v in L if v!=bg])

            ext=[]

# Hypothesis: each color shoots a single diagonal ray (away from its cluster centroid) to edge.
I=G['Demo pair 5 input']; O=G['Demo pair 5 output']
H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
def solve(g):
    g=[row[:] for row in g]; Hh,Ww=len(g),len(g[0])
    import collections
    pts=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for r in range(Hh):
        for c in range(Ww):
            if g[r][c]!=1: pts[g[r][c]].append((r,c))
    res=[row[:] for row in g]
    for v,ps in pts.items():
        mr=sum(p[0]/len(ps) for p in ps); mc=sum(p[1]/len(ps) for p in ps)
        # direction = unit vector from centroid through median/farthest? use pixel farthest from centroid, choose sign
        def dist(p): return abs(p[0]-mr)+abs(p[1]-mc)
        far=max(ps,key=dist)
        dr=1 if far[0]>mr else -1 if far[0]<mr else 0
        dc=1 if far[1]>mc else -1 if far[1]<mc else 0
        rr,cc=far
        while True:
            rr+=dr; cc+=dc
            if not(0<=rr<Hh and 0<=cc<Ww): break
            res[rr][cc]=v
    return res
out=solve(I)
print(out==O)

def load():

        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G

def solve(g,bg=None):
    g=[row[:] for row in g]; Hh,Ww=len(g),len(g[0])
    pts={(r,c):g[r][c] for r in range(Hh) for c in range(Ww) if g[r][c]!= (bg if bg else g[0][0])}
    # bg = most common value
    import collections
    vals=collections.Counter(g[r][c] for r in range(Hh) for c in range(Ww)); bg=vals.most_common(1)[0][0]
    pts={k:v for k,v in pts.items()}
    allp=list(pts)
    MR=sum(p[0] for p in allp)/len(allp); MC=sum(p[1] for p in allp)/len(allp)
    res=[row[:] for row in g]
    for (r,c) in pts:
        v=g[r][c]
        dr=(r>MR)-(r<MR); dc=(c>MC)-(c<MC)
        rr,cc=r,c
        while True:

            if not(0<=rr<Hh and 0<=cc<Ww): break
            if res[rr][cc]==bg: res[rr][cc]=v
    return res
